To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) 11-12 years old is a critical age group for HPV vaccine uptake and physicians are not discussing it frequently enough; and (2) physicians who do not discuss the vaccine frequently are more likely to be family physicians, male, report that parents will not accept it if discussed with other recommended vaccines and express concern about the possibility of waning immunity.

(1) pediatricians and family medicine physicians (FP) strongly recommend HPV vaccination for girls, but less so for boys; (2) more than one-half of pediatricians and FP reported ≥25% parents deferring HPV vaccination; (3) more than one-third of pediatricians and one-half of FP rarely or occasionally discuss HPV vaccination at 11-12 years well visit; (4) compared with physicians who frequently or always discuss HPV vaccination, those who rarely or occasionally do so are

1) pediatricians and FP strongly recommend HPV vaccination for girls and boys at 11-12 years, 2) more than one-half of physicians reported that at least 25% of parents defer HPV vaccination, 3) 84% of pediatrics and 75% FP frequently/always discussed HPV vaccine at the 11- 12 year well visit.
